hook.line: Tomás wants to tell Vale she can drop by *any* day, and later to say that the morning Altamira came was just an *ordinary* one. In English that is two different words. In Spanish it is one word, and the only thing that changes is which side of the noun it sits on.

examples.es: Cualquier persona puede entrar al café.
examples.en: Anyone can come into the café.
You can come at any time. (to a friend)

examples.es: Es un tinto cualquiera, nada especial.
examples.en: It's an ordinary coffee, nothing special.

rule:
Before the noun, *cualquier* means *any*: you choose, it makes no difference. *Cualquier día*, *cualquier hora*.

After the noun, *cualquiera* means *ordinary*: nothing special about it. *Un día cualquiera*, *una tarde cualquiera*.

The shape changes too. Before a noun it is short and the same for masculine and feminine: *cualquier día*, *cualquier persona*. After a noun it keeps its full ending: *un día cualquiera*.

English needs two different words. Spanish uses one word and lets its position carry the meaning.
smallPrint: Teachers call the shortening of *cualquiera* before a noun apocope, the same thing that turns *bueno* into *buen*. The meaning change follows the position of the adjective.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cualquier* or *cualquiera* and type the whole sentence, to say "Come any day" to a friend: *Ven ___ día.*
yourTurn.why: It comes before the noun and means *any*, so the short form *cualquier*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cualquier* or *cualquiera* and type the whole sentence, to say "It was an ordinary day": *Era un día ___.*
yourTurn.why: It comes after the noun and means *ordinary*, so the full form *cualquiera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Anyone can come into the café.
yourTurn.answer: Cualquier persona puede entrar al café.
yourTurn.why: *Cualquier* goes before *persona* and stays short, even though *persona* is feminine.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It was an ordinary afternoon.
yourTurn.why: *Cualquiera* goes after the noun to mean *ordinary*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: You can come at any time.
Turn it into "ordinary": *Fue cualquier martes.* Type: It was an ordinary Tuesday.
yourTurn.why: Moving the word after the noun, with *un*, changes *any* into *ordinary*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into "any": *Era un martes cualquiera.* Type: Any Tuesday will do.
yourTurn.why: Moving the word before the noun, in its short form, changes *ordinary* into *any*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After the noun the word keeps its full ending, *cualquiera*.
Almost. Before a noun the word shortens to *cualquier*, even before a feminine noun.
Almost. *Un día cualquiera* means an ordinary day, so it sounds as if you are inviting someone on a dull one. For "any day you like" put *cualquier* first.

personal: Tell a friend which day they can visit you, with *cualquier*. Then describe a day that was nothing special, with *cualquiera*.
